title: Twinleaf Pharmacy LLM onramp scratchpad
content:
Meeting capture + working notes (very rough)

Context:
- Twinleaf Pharmacy (regional chain) exploring LLM for three features: automated pharmacist triage suggestions, prescription claim explanation to patients (plain-language), and in-store POS assistant for inventory / substitution recommendations.
- Customer insists on private deployment (VPC or on-prem) due to PHI and corporate policy. They have an existing EHR/dispensing backend (Medsys v3) and an SSO (Okta).
- Initial POC: 4 stores, internal staff only, no patient-facing public launch until evals pass.

Attendees (11/02 call):
- Twinleaf: Sarah Kim (CTO), Raj Patel (Head Pharmacy Ops), Denise Wu (Compliance)
- Redwood: Priya Nair (SE), Marcus Alvarez (Solutions Eng), Lena Ortiz (Security PM)
- Later follow-up: Samir Gao (Runtime eng)

High-level asks from Twinleaf:
1) Private deployment pattern that keeps PHI off Redwood hosted control plane (they prefer customer-managed control plane or private deployment).
2) Low latency at POS: < 120ms 95p for short prompts (1-2 sentence completion), typical seq len small.
3) Model determinism / auditability: need request/response logging but with redaction and retention controls.
4) Ability to pin model versions and roll back quickly.
5) Cost estimate for pilot (4 stores, ~2000 queries/day).
6) Integration with Medsys: should be able to fetch medication context (current meds, allergies) for prompt enrichment but not persist PHI in Redwood logs.

Technical constraints noted by Twinleaf:
- 4 stores have limited WAN: 50–100Mbps shared, intermittent spikes during close-of-day syncs.
- Existing datacenter (colocated) runs VMware; ops team can host a small k8s cluster but prefers an appliance if possible.
- Infosec requires HSM-backed KMS for encryption of keys and wants proof of zero-knowledge on our side.
- Auditors want per-request signatures for a 12-month retention window (encrypted-at-rest).

Initial architecture options we discussed:
A) Private (Customer-managed) Control Plane (VPC) + Redwood Runtime in their VPC (recommended during pilot)
   - Pros: satisfy PHI constraints, logs stay in customer account, easier to meet KMS/HSM request, lower legal friction.
   - Cons: customer ops burden; initial templating/installer work.

B) On-prem boxed appliance (future)
   - Not for pilot — longer lead time.

C) Hosted with heavy redaction proxy (not accepted by Twinleaf)

Performance considerations / gotchas:
- POS <120ms target is ambitious if model >3B and on shared VMware; we should recommend a quantized 4/8-bit optimized runtime or batching disabled for POS route.
- KV-caching: benefit for repeated patient context lookups; but cache must be in-customer VPC. Need to document eviction policy.
- Model selection: pick a deterministic, smaller model family for patient-facing explanations to reduce hallucination surface and speed up response.
- Fallbacks: plan for offline deterministic rule-based fallback if runtime unreachable.

Security / compliance items to surface:
- Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM integration required; provide integration runbook for AWS KMS + CloudHSM and Azure Key Vault HSM.
- Logging: log request metadata (hashed identifiers) and redact PHI from textual logs. They want to store raw responses encrypted in their vault; Redwood should not retain plaintext.
- Data residency: Twinleaf requires that all inference compute and logs remain in US-east region for pilot.

Integration details (Medsys):
- Medsys API has endpoints: GET /patient/{id}/medications, GET /patient/{id}/allergies, POST /audit-events
- They want us to run a prompt enrichment flow: retrieve meds/allergies, build a short context blob, send to model. The blob itself must not be persisted in Redwood storage.
- Suggestion: use ephemeral KV cache seeded at request time; ensure runtime config set to disable request body persistence.

Prompt sketch (for "explain claim to patient"):
- System: "You are a licensed pharmacist assistant. You will summarize insurance claim info in plain English for a patient. Use no medical advice wording; include a suggested next step: contact pharmacist for clarification. Keep under 80 words."
- User: [claim details redacted] + medication list (token-limited) + plan name (redacted)

Evaluation / success metrics for pilot:
- Accuracy: fewer than 3% factual errors on a 200 prompt eval set (pharmacist-labeled).
- Latency: P95 < 120ms for POS, P95 < 400ms for triage flow.
- Safety: no PHI leakage in logs, zero high-severity hallucinations in evals.
- Ops: deployable in < 4 weeks with customer ops support.

Rough cost thought (back-of-envelope):
- Expected qps: 2000 queries/day = ~0.023 qps average, spikes at store open/close.
- If using a small quantized 7B model on a single A10-like GPU (on prem) for pilot: estimate infra run-rate ~$3k–5k/mo + SE onboarding (~$12k professional services one-time). Need to tighten numbers with infra team.

Open questions / unknowns (actionable):
- Which exact model variant do they prefer (open to recommendation)? Do they require an open-source license baseline? (Sarah hinted they prefer OSS.)
- Disk/IO constraints on their VMware hosts — need readout of available GPUs or suggestion to run on dedicated host.
- Medsys API rate limits and expected payload sizes (Raj to send API swagger).
- Can Twinleaf accept a short window (30s) for async retry if POS flow temporarily slow? They want near-instant UX though.
- Legal wants sample EULA language for private runtime; legal to draft.

Immediate next steps (owners + dates):
1) Marcus: send private-deploy starter checklist + templated terraform / k8s manifest for VPC runtime by 2024-11-12.
2) Sarah (Twinleaf): provide Medsys swagger + sample payloads by 2024-11-08.
3) Lena: draft BYOK runbook sections for AWS/Azure HSM integration and share by 2024-11-15.
4) Priya: create 200-prompt eval set seed (mix of claim explanations, triage questions, POS substitution requests) and propose model candidates (3 options) by 2024-11-10.
5) Samir: verify runtime latency numbers on equivalent VMware spec and deliver microbenchmark notes by 2024-11-14.
6) Legal/CS: draft pilot agreement (PHI/no-retention clause + auditability) — ask Legal for template (internal).

Notes-to-self / reminders:
- Keep prompts short; use system message to limit advice language.
- Add a small deterministic parser step for medication names -> canonical normalized names to reduce hallucination on substitutions. Could be local service pre-model.
- Warn about tokenization: MedSys free-text instructions sometimes long; trim with heuristics.
- Consider shipping a tiny fallback policy (rules engine) for POS to avoid negative UX.

Potential risks:
- Twinleaf ops may struggle with k8s appliance; plan for a managed deployment assist window (3 days on site or remote pairing).
- If we push a larger model for accuracy, POS latency SLA might break. Need to trade-off.
- Audit retention policies may force additional infra cost for encrypted retention and retrieval APIs.

Decisions needed from execs before pilot kickoff:
- Approve a reduced-severity SLA for pilot (no financial penalties) but with uptime targets and support hours.
- Approve SE allocation: 2 weeks full-time + 1 week of runtime eng support.
- Pricing approach: fixed PS + monthly infra + per-token fallback pricing (or fixed monthly pilot price).

End of scratchpad.

-- Priya
summary: Working notes for Twinleaf Pharmacy private onramp. Capture of technical asks, constraints, initial architecture options, evaluation metrics, open questions, owners and next steps. Draft status.
